| 1\. Product Overview |
| :---- |

The proposed product is a Campaign Management and Attendance Verification module for the Sales Ecosystem. It enables business, marketing, CRM/CLM, and field teams to create campaigns or seminars, select target audiences such as carpenters, contractors, engineers, retailers, dealers, or other influencers, submit the campaign/audience list for approval, execute the event, capture attendance with live attendee photo, and verify whether the actual attendee matches the registered participant profile.

The module should support a phased implementation. Phase 1 focuses on campaign creation, audience registration/import, approval, Ready for Execution status, attendance capture, manual CRM/CLM verification, duplicate control, and participant 360 history. Later phases can introduce automated AI-based face matching once verified reference-image data and governance controls are available.

**Primary business outcome**

* Create a controlled digital process for campaign/seminar execution instead of manual lists and fragmented verification.  
* Ensure attendance is tied to the correct registered person through photo/NID/profile comparison.  
* Build reusable campaign participant history, especially for carpenter/influencer engagement and 360-degree profile views.  
* Protect the existing Sales Ecosystem database by using a reference/hybrid architecture until authoritative-source rules are finalized.

| 2\. Problem Statement |
| :---- |

Business teams need to conduct carpenter/influencer campaigns and seminars, but the current process discussed in the meeting lacks a confirmed end-to-end system for campaign planning, audience approval, attendance capture, identity verification, and historical performance tracking. Existing participant or influencer data may be spread across Sales Ecosystem records, manually maintained lists, and business-provided databases. This creates duplicate risk, manual verification burden, poor traceability, and weak post-campaign analytics.

The meeting also highlighted uncertainty around whether the campaign database should directly modify the existing Sales Ecosystem database or remain segregated as a reference database. Without a clear model, campaign execution may either corrupt core operational records or fail to leverage existing influencer/dealer/retailer data effectively.

| Problem framing The problem is not only “registering carpenters.” The stronger product problem is campaign execution governance: who is invited, who is approved, who actually attended, how the attendee was verified, and how that history is reused for future engagement. |
| :---- |

| 3\. Goals |
| :---- |

| ID | Goal | Description | Success Measure |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| G1 | Digitize campaign lifecycle | Campaign can move from Draft to Approved to Ready for Execution to Completed with audit trail. | 100% of campaigns follow controlled status flow. |
| G2 | Enable controlled audience selection | Users can select/import campaign audiences by configured audience type. | Support manual entry, CSV upload, and API-based import where source data is available. |
| G3 | Improve attendance reliability | Every attendance record should be tied to a registered/listed participant and captured with live photo. | \>=95% of attendance records have photo and participant mapping in pilot. |
| G4 | Introduce manual verification in MVP | CRM/CLM can compare live attendee photo with NID/profile/reference image and mark Verified/Rejected. | \>=90% of captured attendance verified within agreed SLA after execution. |
| G5 | Build participant 360 history | Maintain campaign attendance, verification, approval, and participation history per influencer/person. | 360 profile available for all registered campaign participants. |
| G6 | Reduce duplicate participant risk | Duplicate checks on registration/import based on mobile/NID/name/company/source reference where available. | Duplicate exception queue created; duplicate rate tracked. |
| G7 | Prepare for AI verification later | Collect structured, consented, high-quality image/reference data for future face verification feasibility. | AI readiness checklist completed before Phase 2/3 decision. |

| 4\. Non-Goals |
| :---- |

* Phase 1 will not deliver fully automated AI face recognition or face-matching decisions. Manual verification is the MVP default.  
* The module will not replace the full Sales Ecosystem master-data governance process.  
* The module will not include inbound logistics, truck hiring, or logistics execution workflows; those were explicitly treated as a separate topic in the discussion.  
* The MVP will not finalize incentive payout, gift distribution settlement, budget accounting, or marketing ROI ledger unless separately approved.  
* The MVP will not infer identity from a photo without human verification and business-approved governance.  
* The MVP will not directly overwrite core Sales Ecosystem influencer/dealer/customer records without an approved source-of-truth and integration rule.  
* The PRD does not confirm exact company/business-unit names where the transcript was unclear; those must be validated by business stakeholders.

| :---- |

**Internal users**

| Reporting Viewer / Management | Leadership and business reviewers. | Review campaign execution, attendance, verification, and participant 360 reports. |

**External audience/participant types**

* Carpenters: primary audience repeatedly referenced in the meeting, including the concept of “Carpenter 360.”  
* Contractors and engineers: discussed as additional stakeholder/audience types for campaign or seminar targeting.  
* Retailers, dealers, clients, and other influencers: discussed as possible multi-audience categories requiring validation.  
* Unlisted walk-in participants: handling is not confirmed and remains an open question.

| 6\. Problem Validation |
| :---- |

Validation is currently qualitative and meeting-derived. The transcript repeatedly identifies the need to manage campaigns/seminars, maintain a reference database, approve audiences before execution, capture attendance, compare live attendee photo with NID/profile images, and later explore AI-enabled face verification.

| Validation Source | Observed Need | Product Implication |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Meeting evidence | Campaign/seminar execution requires an audience list, approval, readiness status, attendance, and verification. | Supports end-to-end campaign lifecycle requirement. |
| Data concern | Existing Sales Ecosystem and reference data may be separate; direct impact on Sales Ecosystem should be avoided until architecture is confirmed. | Supports reference/hybrid database approach. |
| Verification concern | Business wants confidence that the attendee is the correct person, using NID/profile/live photo comparison. | Supports manual verification queue and photo capture. |
| Future ambition | AI analysts/developers and automated face detection were discussed as a desired future state. | Supports phased roadmap rather than MVP overreach. |
| Operational concern | Readiness for execution and attendance were discussed as separate stages. | Supports formal campaign statuses and transition criteria. |

| 7\. Proposed Solutions |
| :---- |

| ID | Solution | Mechanism | Importance | Feasibility |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| S1 | MVP Campaign Workflow | Create campaigns, select audience, submit for approval, move to Ready for Execution, capture attendance, complete verification. | High | High |
| S2 | Reference/Hybrid Participant Database | Maintain campaign participants in a controlled reference database, linked to Sales Ecosystem records when available. | High | Medium |
| S3 | Manual Attendance Verification | CRM/CLM compares live photo against NID/profile/reference images and marks Verified, Rejected, or Exception. | High | High |
| S4 | Bulk Upload \+ API Import | Allow campaign audience data from CSV and future APIs with duplicate validation and error reports. | High | Medium |
| S5 | Participant 360 Profile | Show campaign history, attendance, verification status, approvals/rejections, and future performance signals. | Medium | Medium |
| S6 | AI Face Verification Readiness | Collect structured photos and design verification data for later AI model integration. | Medium | Low for MVP; High for future |

| Recommended product approach Proceed with S1 \+ S2 \+ S3 as the MVP. Treat AI verification as a later phase after data readiness, privacy governance, and technical feasibility are proven. |
| :---- |

| 8\. User Flow |
| :---- |

The following flow represents the recommended MVP lifecycle derived from the meeting discussion.

![][image1]

**Step-by-step flow**

1. Campaign creator creates a campaign in Draft status with organization/company, campaign type, date/time, venue, objective, and target audience type.  
2. Creator adds participants manually, through CSV bulk upload, or through API/source-data import where available.  
3. System validates required fields and runs duplicate checks before submission.  
4. Creator submits campaign and audience list for approval.  
5. Marketing/business approver reviews campaign/audience details and approves or rejects.  
6. Approved campaign moves to Ready for Execution once venue, audience, and attendance setup are complete.  
7. Event executor opens the Ready campaign and marks attendance during the event.  
8. System captures live attendee photo and links the attendance record to a registered/listed participant.  
9. CRM/CLM verifier reviews photo against NID/profile/reference image and marks Verified, Rejected, or Exception.  
10. Completed campaign updates participant 360 profile and reporting dashboards.

**Feature details and acceptance criteria**

| Feature Area | Acceptance Criteria |
| ----- | ----- |
| Campaign Creation | Given an authorized campaign creator, when the user fills mandatory fields and saves, then the system creates a Draft campaign with unique campaign ID and audit log entry. |
| Audience Upload | Given a campaign in Draft, when the creator uploads a CSV using the approved template, then the system validates mandatory fields, detects duplicates, imports valid rows, and produces an error file for invalid rows. |
| Approval | Given a campaign submitted for approval, when the approver approves, then campaign status changes to Approved or Ready for Execution based on readiness criteria; when rejected, reason is mandatory. |
| Attendance | Given a campaign in Ready for Execution, when the executor marks a participant present, then live photo capture is mandatory before saving attendance. |
| Verification | Given captured attendance with photo, when CRM/CLM reviewer verifies, then the system stores status, reviewer, timestamp, and verification remarks. |
| 360 Profile | Given a participant profile, when a user opens it, then campaign history and verification outcomes are visible subject to RBAC. |

| 10\. Metrics |
| :---- |

**North Star Metric**

**Verified Campaign Attendance Rate \= Verified attendance records / Total captured attendance records. This directly measures whether campaign execution produces trustworthy attendance data.**

| Level | Metric | Formula / Definition | Why It Matters |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| North Star | Verified Campaign Attendance Rate | Verified attendance / captured attendance | Core trust metric for campaign execution. |
| L1 | Campaign Execution Completion Rate | Completed campaigns / approved campaigns | Indicates whether approved campaigns are actually executed. |
| L1 | Approval Cycle Time | Submission to approval duration | Measures process bottlenecks. |
| L1 | Attendance Capture Completeness | Attendance records with live photo / total attendance | Validates execution data quality. |
| L1 | Verification SLA Compliance | Records verified within SLA / total records needing verification | Tracks CRM/CLM workload and responsiveness. |
| L2 | Duplicate Exception Rate | Duplicate exceptions / total imported or added participants | Measures data quality risk. |
| L2 | Rejected Attendance Rate | Rejected verifications / total verified records | Identifies mismatch or fraud/quality issues. |
| L2 | Import Success Rate | Successfully imported rows / total uploaded rows | Measures template and data-readiness quality. |
| L2 | Participant 360 Coverage | Participants with complete profile/history / total participants | Tracks completeness of campaign intelligence. |

| 11\. Technical Considerations |
| :---- |

**Conceptual architecture**

![][image2]

| Area | Consideration |
| ----- | ----- |
| Architecture | Use a modular service for campaign management. Prefer a reference/hybrid database initially to prevent uncontrolled modification of Sales Ecosystem master data. |
| Integration | Read/link existing Sales Ecosystem participant/dealer/retailer/influencer data where available. API availability and data structure must be assessed before final timeline. |
| Media storage | Store attendee photos and reference images securely with access control, encryption at rest, controlled retention, and signed/private access URLs. |
| Identity data | NID/reference image handling must be access-controlled and auditable. Only authorized verifiers should view sensitive images. |
| RBAC | Different permissions are required for campaign creator, approver, executor, verifier, admin, and viewer roles. |
| Auditability | Every status change, import, approval, rejection, verification, and participant profile update must be logged. |
| Duplicate engine | Initial duplicate check can be rule-based; future enhancement can include fuzzy matching. Manual exception handling is required. |
| Performance | Bulk upload should process large participant files asynchronously if row count exceeds agreed threshold. |
| Offline/poor network | If event sites face weak connectivity, attendance capture may require offline draft mode; this is recommended but requires technical validation. |
| AI readiness | Face verification should not be promised until reference-image quality, model accuracy, bias risk, consent, and human review process are validated. |

| 12\. Challenges and Risks |
| :---- |

| ID | Risk | Description | Mitigation |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| R1 | Scope creep | Campaign, CRM, AI, attendance, and logistics topics may get mixed into one release. | Define MVP scope and keep logistics separate. |
| R2 | Transcript ambiguity | Some meeting terms and org names are unclear. | Validate PRD with stakeholders before backlog finalization. |
| R3 | Data-source uncertainty | Existing Sales Ecosystem data/API structure may increase development effort. | Run technical discovery before committing delivery date. |
| R4 | Duplicate participants | Manual entry and uploads may create duplicate carpenters/influencers. | Mandatory duplicate checks and exception queue. |
| R5 | Manual verification bottleneck | CRM/CLM may face high workload after large campaigns. | SLA, queue prioritization, and batch verification UX. |
| R6 | Photo quality failure | Poor attendee photo quality may block verification. | Photo capture guidelines and retake workflow. |
| R7 | Sensitive data exposure | NID and face images are sensitive personal data. | RBAC, audit log, secure media storage, and retention policy. |
| R8 | AI overcommitment | Automated face verification may not be feasible in MVP. | Treat AI as future phase with feasibility gate. |
| R9 | Approval ambiguity | Unclear whether approval applies to campaign, audience list, or individual participants. | Confirm approval object and status transitions. |

| 13\. Launch Plan |
| :---- |

| Launch Stage | Activities | Exit Criteria |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Phase 0: Discovery & Sign-off | Confirm scope, roles, campaign status model, audience types, data architecture, required fields, and approval flow. | Signed PRD, field dictionary, workflow diagram, architecture decision. |
| Phase 1: MVP Build | Build campaign creation, audience selection/upload, duplicate checks, approval, Ready for Execution, attendance photo capture, manual verification, audit log, basic reports. | UAT-ready MVP. |
| Phase 2: Pilot | Run controlled pilot with one business unit/campaign type and limited users. | Pilot report with adoption, verification SLA, data-quality findings. |
| Phase 3: Full Rollout | Roll out to additional organizations/campaign types after configuration and training. | Production rollout checklist completed. |
| Phase 4: Optimization | Improve import APIs, 360 analytics, reporting, exception handling, and AI feasibility preparation. | Roadmap backlog and AI readiness gate. |

**Pre-launch checklist**

* Business confirms audience categories and approval matrix.  
* Engineering confirms reference database vs direct integration approach.  
* CSV template finalized and tested with real sample data.  
* CRM/CLM verification team trained on verification statuses and rejection reasons.  
* Photo capture, NID/reference image viewing, and sensitive-data access tested under RBAC.  
* UAT includes duplicate upload, approval rejection, attendance retake, and verification exception cases.

| 16\. Open Questions |
| :---- |

11. Is the module officially carpenter-only, or should it be designed as generic campaign management for multiple audience types?  
12. What are the final audience categories for MVP?  
13. Should campaign audience selection be single-select or multi-select?  
14. Who can create a campaign, and who can approve it?  
15. Does approval apply to the campaign, the participant list, individual attendees, or all three?  
16. What exact fields are mandatory for campaign creation?  
17. What exact fields are mandatory for participant registration?  
18. Will participants be created directly in this module, imported from Sales Ecosystem, or both?  
19. What is the authoritative source for carpenter/contractor/influencer data?  
20. Which reference image should be used for verification: NID photo, profile photo, previous attendance photo, or another source?  
21. Can unlisted walk-in participants be added during execution?  
22. What happens when a participant is rejected after attendance is captured?  
23. What is the CRM/CLM verification SLA?  
24. What reports are mandatory for management on day one?  
25. What privacy/retention rules apply to NID and face photos?  
26. What is the agreed delivery timeline after engineering discovery?

| 17\. Trade-Offs |
| :---- |

| Trade-off | Consideration | Recommendation |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Manual verification first vs AI first | Manual verification is slower but feasible and controllable. AI first could be faster later but has technical/privacy/model-risk uncertainty. | Use manual verification in MVP; design data foundation for AI. |
| Reference DB vs direct Sales Ecosystem update | Reference DB reduces operational risk but may duplicate data. Direct update improves single source of truth but may corrupt core records without governance. | Hybrid approach: reference DB with controlled links and later sync rules. |
| Generic campaign module vs carpenter-only module | Generic model is more scalable but takes more design effort. Carpenter-only is faster but may need rework. | Design generic audience model while configuring carpenter as MVP audience. |
| Strict duplicate blocking vs warning | Blocking improves data quality but can slow field execution. Warning improves speed but may increase duplicates. | Block high-confidence duplicates; route uncertain duplicates to exception queue. |
| Full 360 profile vs basic history | Full profile gives better analytics but depends on source integration. Basic history is faster. | Start with campaign history; expand to performance/order data in later phase. |

| ID | Requirement Area | Requirement Statement | Priority |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| FR-001 | Campaign creation | System shall allow authorized users to create campaigns with campaign type, title, organization, date/time, venue, objective, owner, and audience type. | High |
| FR-002 | Draft save | System shall allow incomplete campaigns to be saved as Draft until mandatory fields are completed. | High |
| FR-003 | Audience management | System shall allow users to add/select participants for a campaign from configured audience categories. | High |
| FR-004 | Bulk upload | System shall support CSV participant upload using approved template and produce validation errors. | High |
| FR-005 | Duplicate check | System shall detect likely duplicates during participant creation/import. | High |
| FR-006 | Submission for approval | System shall allow campaigns and/or audience lists to be submitted for approval. | High |
| FR-007 | Approval action | Approver shall be able to approve, reject, or return for correction with mandatory comments for rejection/return. | High |
| FR-008 | Ready for Execution | Approved campaigns shall move to Ready for Execution only after required readiness criteria are met. | High |
| FR-009 | Attendance capture | Event executor shall be able to mark attendance for listed participants and capture live photo. | High |
| FR-010 | Verification queue | Attendance records requiring verification shall appear in CRM/CLM verification queue. | High |
| FR-011 | Manual verification | Verifier shall be able to compare live photo with reference image and mark Verified, Rejected, or Exception. | High |
| FR-012 | Campaign completion | System shall allow campaign closure only after attendance and verification rules are satisfied or exceptions are documented. | Medium |
| FR-013 | Participant 360 | System shall show participant-level campaign attendance and verification history. | Medium |
| FR-014 | Reporting | System shall provide campaign summary, attendance summary, verification summary, duplicate summary, and pending-action reports. | Medium |
| FR-015 | Audit log | System shall record user, timestamp, action, old value/new value where applicable, and remarks for key actions. | High |
